summary: This program figures out how many pizzas to order for a party by storing the party size, the slices in each pizza, and how many slices each person will eat, then doing the arithmetic and printing all the values back out.

lines.text: All three starting values are whole numbers held in int variables, which is the right choice here because you cannot invite half a person or order a fraction of a pizza. Change any of these three and run the program again to see the order recalculated.
A variable can hold the result of a calculation, not just a value you type in, and that result then becomes an ingredient in the next calculation.

Dividing two ints in Java throws away any remainder, so 20 slices divided by 8 would give 2 pizzas and leave four people hungry. Adding one less than a full pizza before dividing rounds the answer up, which is how a real order works.

The plus sign between text in quotes and a variable joins them into one message rather than adding numbers; Java converts the number to text for you. Printing the inputs alongside the answer lets the customer confirm the order is based on the right assumptions.
